outcome: progression of labour (duration of first and second stages)
mode of birth (vaginal, instrumental vaginal, caesarean section)
cohort: The study included 90 nulliparous parturients with established labour, aged 20-35 years, body weight less than 80 kg, at least 36 completed weeks of gestation, a single fetus in vertex presentation, and cervical dilatation greater than 4 cm.
finding: Epidural analgesia provided increased pain relief and patient satisfaction, shortened the first stage of labour, prolonged the second stage, and showed similar neonatal outcomes and no increase in instrumental vaginal deliveries or cesarean sections compared to no analgesia.
mod_finding: There was no statistically significant difference in the number of vaginal deliveries, instrumental deliveries, or C-sections between the epidural and control groups.
